senses.gloss: m.(b. h.; cmp. קָנַן)calamus, reed; anything resembling a reed, branch of a candlestick; windpipe &c.
units: <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:6:4">Cant. R. to I, 6</cite> (legend about the origin of Rome) <he>ירד … ק׳ גדול וכ׳</he> Michael the archangel came down and planted a large reed in the sea &c.
<cite ref="Taanit 20a:15">Taan. 20ᵃ</cite> <he>לעולם … רך כק׳ וכ׳</he> man must at all times be yielding like a reed and not unbending like a cedar, v. <cite ref="S00348"><he>קוֹלְמוֹס</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 12:14">Tosef. Sabb. XII</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 13:14">XIII</cite>), 14 <he>ק׳ של מנורה</he> the branch of a candlestick; <cite ref="Shabbat 47a:7">Sabb. 47ᵃ</cite> <he>קְנֵה מנורה</he>; Y. ib. XII, 13ᶜ <cite ref="S01567"><he>קְנֵי</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Shabbat 47a:7">Ib.</cite> <he>ק׳ של ציידין</he> a part of the composite pole which the hunters use (to reach the nests); Bab. l. c. <he>קְ׳ סיידין</he> of the whitewashers; Tosef. l. c. <he>ציידין</he> (Var. <cite ref="O00001"><he>ס׳</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 17:16">Kel. XVII, 16</cite> <he>קְ׳ מאזניים</he> the beam of the balance.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 17:16">Ib.</cite> <he>ק׳ של עני וכ׳</he> the poor man’s cane which has a receptacle for water.—<he>דחה בק׳</he>, v. <cite ref="D00397"><he>דָּחָה</he></cite>.—
<cite ref="Berakhot 61a:29">Ber. 61ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>ק׳ מוציא קול</he> the windpipe produces sound.
<cite ref="Chullin 21b">Ḥull. 21ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Zevachim 65b:9">Zeb. 65ᵇ</cite> <he>עד שמגיע … לק׳</he> until he reaches (with his nail) the gullet or the windpipe.
<cite ref="Chullin 28b:2">Ḥull. 28ᵇ</cite> (in Chald. dict.) <he>נבדקיה לק׳ וכ׳</he> let him examine the windpipe and cut it &c.

Men. XI, 6 עשרים … כחצי ק׳ חלול twenty-eight staves shaped like a segment of a hollow reed; a. fr.—Ohol. I, 8 ק׳ = קְנֵה זרוע forearm.—קְנֵה שפה, v. קָמָה.—הושיט בק׳ [to hold forth on a cane,] to treat lightly, consider unimportant.

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 8:9">Num. R. s. 8</cite> end <he>דבר … והושיטו לו בק׳</he> (not <he>והושיטה</he>) something for which that ancestor prostrated himself in prayer (<cite ref="Genesis 28:20">Gen. XXVIII, 20</cite>) …, and now comes this man (Aquila) and holds it up to contempt!; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 123">Yalk. Gen. 123</cite>; <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 70:5">Gen. R. s. 70</cite>.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 70:5">Ib.</cite> <he>את מושיטו לזה בק׳</he> dost thou make it appear contemptible to this man?; <cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 7:8:1">Koh. R. to VII, 8</cite>.—Pl. <he>קָנִים</he>, <cite ref="S01587"><he>קָנִין</he></cite>. Men. l. c. Ib. <he>סידור ק׳</he> the arrangement of the staves between the cakes of the show-bread.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 17:17">Kel. XVII, 17</cite>, a. fr. <he>מחצלת ק׳</he> a reed mat.
<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 35:5">Ex. R. s. 35</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Psalms 68:31">Ps. LXVIII, 31</cite>) <he>חיה הדרה בין הק׳</he> the beast that dwells among the reeds (Rome, v.
<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:6:4">Cant. R. to I, 6</cite>, quoted above).
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 1">Gen. R. s. 1</cite> <he>עשיר … לק׳</he> he is a rich man and needs no reeds (for his house); <he>הרי הוא צריך לקְנֵי המדה</he> he still needs the measuring rods; a. fr.
